reasons.A: Long, clause-laden sentences broken mid-stream by dashes and 'I think' asides, semicolon joins and no contractions come closest to the passage's interruptive, arguing movement; the exclamatory parenthesis is a slight overreach.
reasons.D: Dense paragraphs, 'I fancy', 'Granted;' and dash interruptions fit well, but runs of clipped punchlines ('Nobody could hand it to him. Nobody could take it away.') and a 'didn't' contraction pull away from the author's sustained periodic rhythm.
reasons.C: Has the period diction and parenthetical asides, but leans on short aphoristic sentences and a neat epigrammatic close, with paragraphing far choppier than the author's single dense block.
reasons.B: Plain, evenly paced modern expository prose with no dashes, parentheses, first-person hedges or interruptive clauses; the tone is neutral explanation rather than the author's opinionated, qualifying argument.
